name: Plugin bundle format (.codex-plugin/plugin.json)
what: A plugin is a folder with a JSON manifest that declares identity, marketing metadata, a skills directory, an MCP server file and inline hooks. The app shows it in a plugin store with name, descriptions, icons, brand colour, screenshots and default prompts.
how: Manifest fields observed across nine bundled plugins: name, version, description, author, homepage, repository, license, keywords, skills (directory), mcpServers (path to .mcp.json), hooks (inline object with a nested hooks map), and an interface block (displayName, shortDescription, longDescription, developerName, category, capabilities [Interactive|Read|Write], websiteURL, privacyPolicyURL, termsOfServiceURL, defaultPrompt[], brandColor, composerIcon, logo, logoDark, screenshots[]). Optional assets/ folder. Plugins without an interface block (codex-app-tools, unified-computer-use) are infrastructure-only and not store-facing.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's plugin_packages table is inert; a manifest with a typed interface block plus declared capabilities (Read/Write/Interactive) is a ready template for the manifest schema Verevon's roadmap calls Agent Plugins packaging (section 23.12).
notes: Evidence key: PLUG = resources/plugins/openai-bundled/plugins under the install root C:/Program Files/WindowsApps/OpenAI.Codex_26.1007.2314.0_x64__2p2nqsd0c76g0/app; EXE-STR:L = line number in scratchpad/tmp/cxpe/codex_exe.strings.txt (printable strings of resources/codex.exe); BUILD:file@N = character offset in extract/codex/.vite/build/file; I18N = scratchpad/tmp/cxib/i18n_all.txt (English renderer catalogue from the sibling audit); RES = install resources dir.

name: Plugin = bundle of skills, apps, MCP servers, hooks, templates and scheduled tasks
what: One installable unit can contribute several kinds of capability at once, and the store card shows which kinds it has. The runtime tells the model which capabilities a selected plugin brings.
how: App-server PluginSummary/PluginDetail carry hasSkills, hasMcps, hasApps, hasHooks, appsNeedingAuth, appTemplates, scheduledTasks, onboardingSkill, installPolicy, authPolicy, availability and eligiblePlanTypes. Sources are a tagged enum: local, git (refName, sparse paths), npm (package, registry) and remote (remotePluginId). Rust crate core-plugins (loader, manager, store, marketplace, remote, discoverable, recommended_plugin_install) implements it.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should model a plugin as a multi-capability package (skills + MCP + hooks + scheduled templates) rather than a single manifest blob, so the Model Plane can resolve each part through its existing capability registry.
notes: Field list read from concatenated string literals; exact JSON shapes were not read.

name: Open "Agent Plugins" manifest compatibility and cross-vendor plugin roots
what: Codex can load plugin folders authored for other agent products. Skill discovery treats .codex-plugin, .claude-plugin and .cursor-plugin manifests as namespace roots, and a root plugin.json with an agent-plugins.org schema is accepted.
how: Rust core-plugins/agent_plugin_manifest.rs validates a root plugin.json whose $schema is https://agent-plugins.org/schemas/1.0.0/plugin.schema.json: lowercase name (letters, digits, dots, hyphens), repository, license, keywords, author {name,url,email}, and a namespaced extensions object (com.openai). Unknown fields are ignored with a log line. agent_plugin_mcp_overlay.rs maps Agent Plugins MCP servers (stdio, streamable HTTP, SSE) into Codex MCP config. skills/loader/discovery.rs probes .codex-plugin/plugin.json, .claude-plugin/plugin.json and .cursor-plugin/plugin.json to derive the plugin namespace of a skill.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's roadmap already lists Agent Plugins packaging; this confirms the standard is real, shipped in a major client, and that accepting Claude/Cursor plugin layouts is a cheap interoperability win.
notes: Quality 4 because validation is strict but the standard itself is young.

name: Marketplace manifest and multi-source plugin registry
what: A marketplace is a catalogue of plugins that can live in a local folder, a Git repo, a URL or npm. Users add more marketplaces, see per-plugin install policy, and can upgrade them in place.
how: Bundled file resources/plugins/openai-bundled/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json: name, interface.displayName, plugins[] each with name, source {source:local,path}, policy {installation:AVAILABLE, authentication:ON_INSTALL}, category (Developer Tools, Engineering, Productivity, Education & Research, Research). Runtime parser RawMarketplaceManifest supports plugin source objects Url, Npm, GitSubdir and Local. App-server methods marketplace/add, marketplace/upgrade, plugin/list, plugin/read, plugin/install, plugin/uninstall, plugin/installed, plugin/search.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs a registry source abstraction (git/url/npm/local) with signed-catalogue semantics; Codex shows the minimal viable shape.

name: Marketplace source restrictions and reserved namespaces
what: An admin can lock the app to an allow-list of marketplace sources; plugins from unlisted marketplaces cannot be installed. OpenAI-owned marketplace names cannot be claimed by third parties.
how: marketplace_policy.rs validates configured marketplaces (source_type local|git, source, ref, sparse_paths, last_updated, last_revision). Error strings: "must be added to config before plugins can be installed while marketplace source restrictions are enabled", allowed-source entries with host_pattern/path/url, "local path must be absolute". Reserved names: openai-curated, openai-api-curated, openai-bundled, openai-bundled-alpha, openai-primary-runtime ("is reserved and cannot be added from this source"). Marketplace manifest name must match the managed marketplace name.
verevonRelevance: Directly relevant to Verevon's enterprise posture (Control Plane owns orgs): an org-level allow-list of plugin sources plus reserved first-party namespaces is the right governance primitive.

name: Atomic marketplace upgrade with backup and rollback
what: Marketplaces can be upgraded individually or all at once; a failed upgrade restores the previous version instead of leaving a half-installed catalogue.
how: core-plugins/marketplace_upgrade/activation.rs: clone into a staging directory (marketplace-upgrade-*), validate the manifest name against the configured marketplace, move the previous root into a marketplace-backup directory, activate, write .codex-marketplace-install.json (source_type, ref_name, sparse_paths, revision), and restore the backup on failure. Detects configuration changes while an upgrade is in flight and refreshes the installed plugin cache afterwards. UI toasts: upgradeSuccess, upgradeAllSuccess, upgradeAllError.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships plugin catalogues, copy the stage-validate-swap-with-backup pattern and the in-flight change detection.

name: npm and Git sourced plugins with safe materialization
what: A plugin can be published as an npm package or a Git subdirectory and installed without running its install scripts.
how: core-plugins/npm_source.rs runs npm pack with --ignore-scripts and --pack-destination, requires exactly one archive, enforces a byte cap, checks package.json name equals the requested package, and extracts into plugins/.marketplace-plugin-source-staging. Git sources use a trusted repository root inside CODEX_HOME with git -c safe.bareRepository=explicit and a scrubbed GIT_* environment (GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_CONFIG*, etc. cleared); a trusted root that escapes the Codex home is rejected.
verevonRelevance: Good model for a hardened plugin fetch path (no lifecycle scripts, name pinning, size cap, repo-root containment) that Verevon's supply-chain checks for skills (roadmap section 24) can reuse.
notes: Line L1311490 is an approximate pointer to the surrounding git-env block; npm lines are exact.

name: Plugin install cache layout and remote install marker
what: Installed plugins are cached per marketplace, plugin and version. Remote (account-hosted) plugins leave a marker file so the cache can be reconciled with the server.
how: $CODEX_HOME/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/ with exactly one version directory per plugin; remote installs write .codex-remote-plugin-install.json containing remote_plugin_id. Cache entries that are stale or invalid are removed during remote_installed_plugin_sync.rs. Skill discovery (cloud-skills container) also scans plugins/cache. Template picker server walks the same layout to find artifact-template-* skills and rejects plugin dirs whose manifest name differs from the directory name.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can adopt a content-addressed per-version cache with a server-reconciled marker instead of mutable in-place plugin rows.

name: Account-hosted remote plugin catalogue, sharing and workspace publishing
what: Besides local marketplaces, plugins can be listed, searched, installed and shared through the ChatGPT backend with global, user and workspace scopes; workspace members can share plugins with each other.
how: core-plugins/remote.rs calls /ps/plugins/list, /ps/plugins/search, /ps/plugins/installed (includeDownloadUrls), /ps/plugins/suggested/codex and /ps/plugins/workspace/shared with pageToken pagination. Scopes GLOBAL, USER, WORKSPACE; listing kinds created-by-me-remote, workspace-directory, workspace-shared-with-me, workspace-shared-with-me-private, workspace-shared-with-me-unlisted. Remote bundles are downloaded and checked against sha256 (remote_bundle.rs). PluginDetail has creatorAccountUserId, sharePrincipals (principalType, principalId), canPublishToWorkspace, shareUrl, discoverability. Methods plugin/share/updateTargets, plugin/share/checkout, plugin/reconcile. A marketplace named openai-curated-remote feeds tool suggestions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's org/Space model maps naturally onto workspace-shared plugins; the principal-based share list and unlisted/private/directory visibility tiers are worth copying.
notes: Behaviour inferred from endpoint literals and struct field names; HTTP schemas not read.

name: Per-plugin installation and authentication policy
what: Each plugin entry declares whether it is installable, whether install must show an interstitial, and when authentication happens. Plans can restrict eligibility and admins can disable a plugin.
how: marketplace.json policy {installation: AVAILABLE, authentication: ON_INSTALL}. App-server fields installPolicy, installPolicySource, mustShowInstallationInterstitial, authPolicy, availability, eligiblePlanTypes, disabledReason; requirements enumerate plugin state AVAILABLE / ENABLED / DISABLED_BY_ADMIN. Plan types seen: free, go, plus, pro, prolite, promax, team, business, enterprise, edu variants.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can gate plugin availability by org plan and require an explicit consent interstitial before the first OAuth/connect step.

name: Signed plugin archives with per-file integrity manifests
what: Bundled plugins ship as signed archives alongside the unpacked tree, so the app can verify that a plugin is the exact release artifact.
how: resources/plugin-signatures/openai-bundled/<plugin>/ contains plugin.tar.gz, plugin.signature.json {algorithm RSA_PKCS1_SHA256, key_id, sha256, signature(base64)} and public-key.der; the tarball contains integrity.json {schema_version 1, hash_algorithm sha256, files[{path, sha256}]}. receipt.json lists every plugin with archive_bytes and sha256 plus environment production, purpose CODEX_DESKTOP_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_SIGNING, CI run_id and source_sha. Verified here: deep-research tarball lists plugin.json, assets, integrity.json and skill files; signature file structure read.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's roadmap wants signed candidate artifacts and skill supply-chain checks; the sha256 file list + detached RSA signature + build receipt is a compact, adoptable scheme.
notes: No code that verifies the signature was found in the JS bundles or by string search of codex.exe, so enforcement and the verifying component are unknown (maybe the MSIX updater or native Rust code). Treat as signing artifact present, enforcement unconfirmed. Quality 3 for that reason.

name: Bundled first-party plugin set (nine plugins) and auto-install with opt-out
what: The app ships browser, chrome, computer-use, unified-computer-use, code-review, codex-app-tools, deep-research, latex and visualize plugins. Browser and computer-use are installed automatically unless the user opted out.
how: The bundled marketplace is copied to $CODEX_HOME/.tmp/bundled-marketplaces/openai-bundled; install state tracked via config plugins.<name>@openai-bundled; bundledPluginOptOutKeys maps browser-use and computer-use to GlobalStateKey *_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_AUTO_INSTALL_DISABLED. Chrome plugin variant depends on build flavor (Dev/InternalAlpha/Nightly/Agent/Prod/PublicBeta) via CODEX_USE_INTERNAL_CHROME_PLUGIN. Forced reload via CODEX_ELECTRON_BUNDLED_PLUGINS_FORCE_RELOAD.
verevonRelevance: A Verevon "first-party plugin" tier (browser, research, docs) distributed as ordinary plugins with an opt-out switch keeps the core small and uses the same loader as third parties.

name: Host patches plugin MCP config at runtime
what: The desktop app rewrites a bundled plugin's .mcp.json and passes config overrides so a plugin's MCP server is enabled only when its prerequisites (Node REPL, browser backend, WSL runtime) exist.
how: main-process function reads .mcp.json of the installed cua_repl plugin, sets enabled, omit_tools_from ([code_mode] or [code_mode, deferred]), env_vars, env (CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES, node paths) and command/args, then atomically writes via tmp file + rename. For codex-app-tools it builds overrides such as plugins.codex-app-tools@openai-bundled.mcp_servers.codex_app.enabled=true when the app-server supports pluginMcpConfigOverrides, otherwise per-server mcp_servers.codex_app.* keys; on WSL it wraps the command with wslpath and WSLENV. Missing prerequisites log reasons missing-pipe, missing-plugin, missing-definition, missing-core-node, missing-windows-runtime.
verevonRelevance: Shows the cost of config-as-plugin-state: Verevon should keep plugin enablement and environment binding in the registry, not in files rewritten at launch.
notes: This runtime mutation of shipped plugin files is a design smell (plugin directory is not immutable) but the atomic tmp+rename mitigates corruption.

name: Plugin capabilities are summarised into the model prompt
what: When a plugin is available (or explicitly selected with @), the model is told what skills, apps and MCP servers it provides and that plugin skills are name-prefixed. The summary is trimmed to fit context.
how: core/src/context renders "Capabilities from the <plugin> plugin" with bullets: tool_search first for the request that explicitly selected the plugin; skills prefixed with the plugin name; apps available in this session; MCP servers available in this session; "Additional plugin capabilities omitted to fit the context limit". Composer sends UserInput::Mention and UserInput::Skill variants; renderer keys pluginMention, skillMention.
verevonRelevance: Verevon injects up to 3 skills by keyword; a per-plugin capability digest plus explicit @-mention semantics ("search its tools before falling back") would make plugin use predictable.

name: Model-initiated plugin and connector install suggestion
what: If the user explicitly asks for a plugin that is not active and tool search found nothing, the model can ask the user to install it; the user accepts, declines or cancels in an inline card.
how: Two tools: list_available_plugins_to_install and request_plugin_install {tool_type connector|plugin, action_type install, tool_id, suggest_reason}. Hard rules in the tool description: only for an exact match to an explicit user request, only after tool search is exhausted, plugin must be in <recommended_plugins>, never in parallel with other tools, root thread only ("can only be used by the root thread"), not available in the TUI. Outcomes accept/decline/cancel; a decline persists a disabled tool suggestion; after install the codex_apps tool cache is refreshed. Server composer endpoints /task_suggestions/dismiss and /composer/items/interactions record interactions.
verevonRelevance: A governed "install on demand" tool is the safe alternative to letting a model enable arbitrary capabilities; Verevon's capability-before-dispatch rule can host the same consent flow.

name: Plugin-shipped scheduled-task templates
what: A plugin can offer ready-made recurring tasks (for example a daily brief) that a user turns into an automation.
how: protocol plugin-scheduled-tasks.ts: template file {name, prompt, schedule} with schedule union hourly {intervalHours, days?}, daily {time}, weekdays {time}, weekly {days[MO..SU], time}; automations carry plugin_template_id. PluginDetail exposes scheduledTasks and appTemplates.
verevonRelevance: Lets Verevon plugins ship routines; combine with a stronger scheduled-run executor (current Verevon runs are single no-tool calls).
notes: Where the template file lives inside a plugin was not found.

name: Plugin MCP overlay hardening
what: Plugin-declared MCP servers are loaded defensively: a plugin cannot point its MCP config outside its own folder, and stdio servers get a private data directory.
how: agent_plugin_mcp_overlay.rs: MCP config must be a regular file; resolved path must stay inside the plugin root ("resolves outside the plugin root; disabling MCP"); stdio servers get a .plugin-data directory (creation failure disables stdio servers); duplicate server names are skipped, manifest object overriding file definitions is logged ("plugin manifest MCP object overwrote an earlier server definition").
verevonRelevance: Apply the same containment checks (path realpath inside plugin root, per-plugin data dir) before Verevon enables any plugin-provided MCP endpoint.

name: Plugin hook declaration and script attribution
what: Plugins can declare lifecycle hooks, and scripts that a plugin runs are attributed to it for metrics.
how: Hooks are read from plugin.json (inline hooks object, shown as plugin.json#hooks[...]) or hooks/hooks.json. script_attribution.rs tags shell/PowerShell runs with plugin identity and a CODEX_PLUGIN_METRICS_OUTPUT sidecar (plugin_metrics_sidecar.rs); telemetry event codex_plugin_measurement_event. Bundled plugins use hook type mcp_tool to call node_repl.turn_ended or cua_repl.turn_ended on Interrupt, SubagentStop and Stop with templated input (hook_event_name, session_id or agent_id, turn_id).
verevonRelevance: Per-plugin usage attribution is exactly what Verevon needs for capability ranking and cost attribution in the registry.
notes: Attribution mechanism read from strings only; precise event fields unknown.

name: Plugin store, install and enablement UX
what: A Skills and Apps hub lists installed and recommended apps, MCP servers, plugins, skills and marketplaces with search; plugins can be enabled, disabled, uninstalled and configured per remote host.
how: Renderer routes /plugins, /plugins/:pluginId, /plugins/:pluginId/app/:toolName, /skills, /skills/manage, /settings/plugins-settings, /settings/mcp-settings and per-host /settings/plugins-settings/hosts/:hostId/plugins/:pluginId (verified in app-initial bundle). Strings: My Apps, My MCPs, My Skills, Recommended, Marketplaces; toasts for enable, disable, uninstall, install error, OAuth timeout, "Plugin changed, but skills couldn't refresh. Reload skills before starting a new chat". sendRequest invalidates MCP status cache after plugin/install or plugin/uninstall.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no plugin install surface; the five-tab hub with per-host settings is a practical IA to copy.
notes: Routes verified by string match in app-initial-b8e1c8014bb4.js.

name: Composer mentions for skills, plugins and apps
what: Typing $ or @ in the composer lists skills, plugins and apps with their source (Built-in, Admin installed, Project, Local file, From plugin) and inserts a typed mention.
how: composer.skillMentionList strings: adminSource, builtInSource, localFileSource, pluginSource ("Plugin: {pluginId} - {path}"), projectSource, fromPlugin, loading, noResults; UserInput::Skill and UserInput::Mention items in turn/start; fuzzyFileSearch for file mentions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's composer has /file /image /search /research /schedule only; add typed skill/app mentions with provenance labels.

name: Skill package format (SKILL.md + agents/openai.yaml)
what: A skill is a folder with a Markdown entry file whose YAML front matter names and describes it; an optional YAML sidecar gives UI metadata and invocation policy. Scripts, references, assets and tests sit beside it.
how: Front matter schema: name (non-empty), description, optional metadata.short-description. Sidecar agents/openai.yaml (or SKILL.json fallback): interface {display_name, short_description, icon_small, icon_large, brand_color, default_prompt}, policy {allow_implicit_invocation, products}, dependencies (tool and OAuth entries). Metadata files are capped at 1 MiB. Optional directories scripts/, references/, assets/, tests/. Bundled examples: deep-research (references/*.md), visualize (scripts, widgets, examples), latex (scripts + Python tests), hatch-pet (17 Python scripts, 4 tests, references).
verevonRelevance: Verevon skills have trigger keywords and file patterns but no package layout; adopt a folder package with progressive disclosure and a UI/policy sidecar so skills can ship scripts and references.

name: Skill discovery roots, limits and concurrency
what: Skills are found in the open project, the user's agents folder, the Codex home and the plugin cache; the scan is bounded so a huge repo cannot stall startup.
how: Hosted skill reader runs a bash pipeline inside the execution container: for roots "$1" (project cwd), $HOME/.agents/skills, ${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills and ${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/plugins/cache it runs ripgrep --files --hidden --glob SKILL.md excluding .git and node_modules, caps at 512 results (head -z -n 512), parses 8 files concurrently, 10 s timeout, errors collected per path ("Unable to read skill metadata"). Skill scope is repo when inside the cwd else user. Rust loader adds a traversal limit ("skills scan reached its traversal limit"), project_root_markers for the project root, and a skills.agents source.
verevonRelevance: Same bounded-scan design suits Verevon Space workspaces: scan roots, hard caps and per-path error reporting.

name: Skill authority and locator model (host, cloud, executor, custom)
what: The same skill catalogue can mix skills on the user's disk, skills in the cloud account, skills inside a remote execution environment and skills from custom providers, each addressed by a typed locator.
how: codex-skills-extension models skill provenance as authority (host, cloud, executor) and locators file, executor package, cloud package and custom resource. Model tools skills.list (cursor pagination, per-authority) and skills.read (package + optional skill:// resource id; root aliases resolved from a "Skill roots" section; executor-backed skills expose skill_root to locate bundled scripts). Cloud skills have their own catalogue cache and fingerprint ("cloud skill cache changed during read" aborts the read); executor skills require filesystem access bound to an environment.
verevonRelevance: Verevon sandboxes (Space-scoped) and learned skills (session-core) are different authorities; a typed locator plus read-by-resource tool would unify them and give skills access to bundled scripts inside a sandbox.
notes: Read from embedded tool descriptions and error strings; no schemas.

name: Skill catalogue context budget with truncation signalling
what: The model sees a bounded skill list; when many skills exist, descriptions are shortened and, past a threshold, removed, and the model is told how many were omitted and that explicit mentions still work.
how: render.rs/render_observability.rs: SkillMetadataBudget, messages "Exceeded skills context budget. All skill descriptions were removed...", "additional N omitted from this bounded skills list", "truncated skill metadata to fit skills context budget"; metrics codex.thread.skills.enabled_total, kept_total, truncated, description_truncated_chars; world-state updates inject "## Host skills update", "## Cloud skills update" and "## Skills update" diffs when availability changes ("No host skills are currently available", "Host skills are available but omitted ... because the skills context budget was exceeded"). Catalog budget is split between host and cloud (CatalogBudgetAllocation totalBudget, cloudLimit).
verevonRelevance: Verevon injects up to 3 skills by character budget with reattach_skill; emitting explicit "update" messages and omission counts would make skill availability auditable to the model and the user.

name: Dynamic skill selection (retrieval over the skill catalogue) in shadow mode
what: Instead of listing every skill, Codex is testing retrieval that picks the few relevant skills per turn. Experiments run in shadow mode and only measure how much the list could shrink.
how: skills/dynamic_skill_selector (character_ngram.rs, multi_query_lexical.rs, rrf_lexical_char.rs) and shadow_selection_experiment/mod.rs. Method ids found: lru_v1, fielded_bm25_v1, character_ngram_v1, lru_plus_lexical_v1, rrf_lexical_char_v1 (reciprocal-rank fusion), weighted_lexical_v1, multi_query_lexical_v1, routing_card_exact_v1, character_routing_card_v1, lru_plus_character_routing_v1, lru_plus_lexical_character_routing_v1, task_context_fusion_v1. Query script classes none|other|cjk|ascii_latin|mixed; telemetry codex.skills.shadow_selection.{duration_ms,catalog_entries,selected_entries,query_terms,reduction_bps,rank}. A stop-word list is embedded.
verevonRelevance: Verevon matches skills by trigger keywords; the fusion of lexical, character n-gram and recency methods, evaluated in shadow before enabling, is a low-risk upgrade path with built-in measurement.
notes: Experiment only; not evidence that any method is enabled in production. Quality 3 for that reason.

name: Implicit vs explicit skill invocation policy
what: Skills are auto-selectable by default; a skill can opt out so it only runs when the user types $name. Skills can also be limited to products.
how: agents/openai.yaml policy.allow_implicit_invocation (bundled deep-research sets true; skill-creator documents false for explicit-only skills) and policy.products (CHATGPT, CODEX, ATLAS enum strings). Explicit mention telemetry distinguishes invoke_type explicit, implicit, unattributed and unknown.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same switch to keep high-risk or costly skills (browser, research fan-out) from being injected automatically.

name: Skill telemetry and attribution (codex.skill.injected)
what: Each time a skill is put in front of the model, an event records which skill, whether the user named it, which plugin it came from and which model and effort ran it.
how: Metric/event codex.skill.injected with fields status, skill, invoke_type (explicit|implicit|unattributed|unknown), plugin_id, model_slug, reasoning_effort. Also codex.skills.shadow_selection.* for the retrieval experiment and codex.thread.skills.* budget counters.
verevonRelevance: Feeds Verevon's existing skill scorecard/quarantine idea with a ready event schema keyed by invoke type and model.

name: Skill approvals as a distinct approval category
what: Running a skill's scripts or reading its resources can require its own approval, separate from shell commands and MCP calls.
how: GranularApprovalConfig fields: sandbox_approval, skill_approval, request_permissions, mcp_elicitations (approval_policy value "granular" next to untrusted, on-request, never). Also fragment <resource_access> in skill read prompts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's capability policy could treat skill execution as its own governed capability class rather than folding it into code_interpreter.
notes: Behaviour of skill_approval inferred from the field name; not traced.

name: Embedded system skills installed into CODEX_HOME/skills/.system
what: Codex ships core skills inside the binary and installs them at startup: image generation, Codex self-documentation, review agent, skill creator, skill installer, Word documents, presentations, spreadsheets and PDF.
how: Front-matter blocks embedded in codex.exe: imagegen, openai-docs ("Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge"), review-agent (read-only defect-first review for delegated reviews), skill-creator, skill-installer, documents/presentations/spreadsheets/pdf. Startup logs "failed to install system skills"; "skills cache cleared (N entries)".
verevonRelevance: A self-knowledge skill (openai-docs) that answers questions about the product's own settings and automations is a cheap, effective support feature for Verevon.

name: skill-installer: curated list and GitHub installs
what: The agent can install skills for the user from a curated catalogue or from any GitHub repo path (including private repos) into the skills folder.
how: System skill skill-installer: "Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path"; resources/skills/skills/.curated holds hatch-pet and onboard-new-user; app-server skills/tree/main reference to a GitHub skills tree and skills/public.
verevonRelevance: Install-from-Git for skills implies a trust model Verevon must define first (signing, scorecard) before allowing agent-driven installs.
notes: Installer script internals not read.

name: skill-creator doctrine: progressive disclosure and minimal skills
what: Codex ships guidance that teaches the agent to write lean skills: three-stage disclosure, scripts only when deterministic, no README clutter, explicit-only skills only on request.
how: System skill text: disclose in stages (name+description, SKILL.md body, references/scripts/assets); keep description discriminating; use scripts/ for repeated logic, references/ for conditional detail, assets/ for output files; naming lowercase-hyphen under 64 chars; init_skill.py <name> --path ... --resources scripts,references,assets and generate_openai_yaml.py --interface key=value; "Approval to complete a task does not expand its scope or execution permissions."
verevonRelevance: Verevon's learned-skill review (sessionreview) should adopt these authoring rules as its rubric so auto-learned skills stay short, scoped and non-permissive.
notes: The scope-limiting rule is notable: skills must not imply permission for extra external actions.

name: Skills that depend on other skills with a hard failure contract
what: A skill can require a companion skill and must stop rather than degrade silently if it is missing.
how: deep-research SKILL.md: use $documents to build and verify the DOCX; if unavailable ask the user to enable the Documents plugin and stop, preserving notes; never substitute Markdown/PDF/chat; "Never describe a file as visually verified unless the rendered pages were actually inspected." hatch-pet delegates all image generation to $imagegen and forbids direct Image API calls.
verevonRelevance: Declare skill-to-skill dependencies and failure contracts in the manifest so Verevon workflows fail loudly instead of returning off-spec output.

name: Skills carry scripts, tests and QA artifacts (skills as software)
what: Complex skills ship deterministic Python helpers with unit tests and validation reports, not just prose.
how: latex plugin: compile_latex.py, detect_tectonic.py, detect_texlive.py, install_texlive.py, latex_doctor.py plus tests (test_compile_latex_strategy.py, test_detect_tectonic.py, test_install_texlive_profile.py). hatch-pet: 17 scripts (assemble_extended_atlas, validate_atlas, make_contact_sheet, measure_direction_continuity, validate_direction_blind_verdicts...) and 4 tests covering chroma decontamination, direction acceptance policy and blind consensus.
verevonRelevance: Supports Verevon's "skills as versioned packages with scorecards" direction: tests inside the package are the strongest quality signal.

name: Skill enablement config and change notifications
what: Users can switch individual skills on or off by path or name, and clients are told when the skill set changes.
how: App-server skills/list (with extraRoots and cwds), skills/config/write (exactly one of path or name), notification skills/changed; skills.shadow_selection and skills.selected_skill_instructions config entries; the desktop invalidates the skill list after plugin changes.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can expose enable/disable per skill per user/org with a push notification when the registry changes.

name: Code mode: model writes JavaScript that orchestrates tools in a V8 isolate
what: Instead of one tool call per round trip, the model can submit a short JavaScript program that calls many tools, aggregates results and returns compact text or images.
how: Tool exec takes raw JS (optional first-line pragma // @exec: {"yield_time_ms":..., "max_output_tokens":...}); runs in a fresh V8 isolate as an async module with no Node, no filesystem, no network, no console; nested tools are on a global tools object (for example await tools.exec_command(...), MCP tools as tools.mcp__server__tool); helpers text(), image(), audio(), generatedImage(), store()/load() for cross-call state, notify(), setTimeout/clearTimeout, ALL_TOOLS, yield_control(), exit(). tool_search is callable from JS. A separate process codex-code-mode-host (V8) speaks a versioned protocol (HostHello, SessionReady, ExecutionStarted, CellClosed, DelegateRequest::InvokeTool and ::Notify) with an optional in-process fallback (disable_in_process_fallback). Plugin .mcp.json can hide tools from code mode via omit_tools_from.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's roadmap lists MCP code mode (section 23.4) as greenfield; Codex shows a concrete contract: isolate without I/O, tools as async functions, persisted store/load, yield control and token-capped output.
notes: Largest single capability gap for Verevon among extensibility features.

name: Deferred tool loading with BM25 tool_search
what: Large tool catalogues are not listed up front; the model searches them on demand and the matching tools become callable.
how: Tool tool_search (also exposed in code mode as tools.tool_search({query, limit: 8})) returns BM25-ranked matches with callable names and TypeScript declarations. MCP server config key omit_tools_from ["deferred"] excludes a server's tools from the eager list; ToolRegistryConfig has error_on_tool_collisions, excluded tool namespaces, direct_only tools, tool input schema max bytes, and turn_metadata_includes_tool_info. Desktop flags deferCodexAppTools and deferCuaTools switch bundled servers between eager and deferred. tools.cache_write/publish/fetch_uncached metrics for the apps tool cache.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's gateway collapses MCP above 40 tools to mcp_catalog + mcp_call; BM25 search that returns callable declarations is the more capable pattern and works with code mode.

name: Persistent JavaScript REPL exposed as an MCP server (node_repl / cua_repl)
what: Browser and computer-use plugins drive their runtimes through a long-lived JavaScript session where state persists across calls and a turn-end hook cleans up.
how: MCP servers node_repl (browser, chrome, computer-use) and cua_repl (unified-computer-use) expose tools js, js_reset and turn_ended; cua_repl .mcp.json: enabled_tools [js, js_reset, turn_ended], omit_tools_from [code_mode, deferred], startup_timeout_sec 120, js output_token_limit 25000. Desktop injects the node_repl server into thread config at thread/start. Bundled cua_node (node 24.21.0-cua.1) hosts @oai/sky.
verevonRelevance: A persistent session with a turn-ended hook is how Verevon's sandbox/browser grants could keep state per run and release it on interrupt.

name: Lifecycle hook engine with three handler kinds
what: Users, admins and plugins can run commands, MCP tools, prompts or agents at fixed points in a session; hooks can inject context, rewrite tool input and veto actions.
how: hooks crate: events PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, SessionStart (source startup|resume|clear|compact|fork), SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, Stop, Interrupt. Handler config is an internally tagged enum command {command, commandWindows, timeout, async, statusMessage, additionalContextLimit}, mcp_tool {server, tool, input, timeout}, prompt and agent (the last two parse but may be unsupported). Each event takes matcher groups (a matcher field per group). Hook stdin JSON includes session_id, transcript_path, hook_event_name, permission_mode, agent_transcript_path, stop_hook_active, agent_id, agent_type, last_assistant_message, tool_input; large outputs spill to files (output_spill.rs); a PreToolUse result may return updatedInput (error if the rewritten input lacks the string field command). Legacy notify = external program.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's hook engine is real but gateway-memory only and absent in Do mode; Codex shows the complete event set, hook sources by config layer, and the input rewrite contract to target.

name: Hook trust model (trusted hash) and config-layer sources
what: Hooks come from system, user, project, plugin, MDM and cloud layers; project and plugin hooks are untrusted until the user approves, and changed hooks fall back to untrusted.
how: hooks/list returns entries with eventName, matcher, timeoutSecs, statusMessage, additionalContextLimit, sourcePath, pluginId, displayOrder, isManaged, currentHash and trustStatus in {managed, untrusted, trusted, modified}; HookStateToml stores trusted_hash. ConfigLayerSource kinds: system, user, project, mdm, sessionFlags, plugin, cloudRequirements, cloudManagedConfig, legacyManagedConfigFile, legacyManagedConfigMdm. Requirements key allowManagedHooksOnly lets admins forbid all non-managed hooks. UI: Settings > Hooks page.
verevonRelevance: Hash-pinned hook trust plus an admin "managed hooks only" switch is directly usable for Verevon's org-owned hook registry and fixes the "hooks only on browser runs" weakness with a governed source.

name: Slash command catalogue (terminal client) with descriptions
what: The terminal client exposes about fifty slash commands for model, permissions, memory, skills, plugins, hooks, goals, side conversations, worktrees and diagnostics.
how: Descriptions embedded in codex.exe (command names for some entries are inferred from their descriptions), e.g. /model (model and reasoning effort), /permissions, /keymap, /vim, /setup-default-sandbox, /experimental, /auto-review-denials (approve one retry of a recent auto-review denial), /memories, /skills, /import (import setup, this project and recent chats from Claude Code), /hooks, /review, /rename, /archive, /delete, /resume, /fork, /worktree, /app (continue in the Desktop app), /init (create AGENTS.md), /compact, /recap, /plan, /voice, /goal, /agent, /side (ephemeral fork), /copy, /export, /raw, /tui, /diff, /mention, /status, /daemon, /warnings, /cd, /pwd, /usage, /debug-config (config layers and requirement sources), /title, /statusline, /theme, /pets, /mcp (list tools; verbose or login <name>), /apps, /plugins, /logout, /quit, /feedback, /rollout, /ps, /stop, /clear, /test-approval, /subagents.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has /models and /compact in capability-core and five composer commands; this list is a prioritised backlog (especially /goal, /side, /import, /debug-config, /memories).

name: Desktop composer slash menu and command palette
what: The desktop app has a searchable slash command dialog and a command palette with thread, panel and navigation actions.
how: Strings composer.slashCommands.dialogTitle/Description/inputPlaceholder/noResults, composer.feedbackSlashCommand, codex.command.* (newThread, searchChats, toggleSidebar, toggleTerminal, toggleReviewPanel, temporaryChat, importExternalAgent, theme, gitReview...), settings page for keyboard shortcuts; command keymap protocol codex-command-keymap.ts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no command palette (grep confirmed in its UI baseline); the command keymap protocol module is a small, well-scoped design to mirror.

name: External agent config import (Claude Code, Cursor and similar)
what: On first run or from settings, Codex scans for another coding agent's setup and offers to import instructions, settings, skills, plugins, MCP servers, subagents, hooks, commands, memory and recent chats.
how: ExternalAgentConfigMigrationItemType: AGENTS_MD, CONFIG, SKILLS, PLUGINS, MCP_SERVER_CONFIG, SUBAGENTS, HOOKS, COMMANDS, MEMORY, SESSIONS. RPC externalAgentConfig/detect, /import, /import/recordHistory; notifications externalAgentConfig/import/progress and /completed; SQLite external_agent_config_imports (with provider_id); settings external-agent-import-sync-enabled and -item-types (keep imported content in sync). Rust crate external-agent-migration (detect/mod.rs, plugins.rs, service.rs, sessions/append.rs, memory_import.rs) with strings "Migrate MCP servers from ...", "Migrate recent sessions from ...", memory import "not supported for the selected migration source"; skills-cursor path. Plugins migration adds the external marketplace via marketplace/add. Onboarding shows hook counts per source.
verevonRelevance: Importing a competitor's setup is an adoption lever; Verevon could import Claude/ChatGPT export data and skills the same way (Verevon UI baseline notes no importer exists).
notes: Which external agents are supported beyond Claude Code (string hits for Cursor skills) is not fully enumerated.

name: Instruction files: AGENTS.md hierarchy, overrides and size limits
what: Project instructions are read from AGENTS.md (with local override variants) up to a byte cap; /init creates one; imports migrate other agents' instruction files.
how: Config defaults show project_doc_max_bytes = 32768 and project_doc_fallback_filenames = []; AGENTS.override.md recognised; ThreadStart returns instruction_sources; developer_instructions, additionalDeveloperInstructions (requirements) and compact_prompt are configurable; model_instructions_file in profiles.
verevonRelevance: Verevon injects org/Space/persona instructions in chat but not Do mode; returning the list of instruction sources to the client is a transparency win worth copying.

name: MCP client built on the Rust MCP SDK (stdio and streamable HTTP)
what: Codex connects to local (stdio) and remote (streamable HTTP) MCP servers and speaks several protocol revisions, including a newer draft, with request timeouts and task/sampling support.
how: codex-rmcp-client and codex-mcp crates on top of rust-sdk (rmcp). Negotiated versions seen: 2024-11-05, 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25, and an InputRequiredResult path that "requires negotiated protocol version 2026-07-28 or newer". Methods in the handler tables: sampling/createMessage, prompts/get, resources/read, resources/subscribe/unsubscribe, tasks/get, tasks/update, tasks/cancel, logging/setLevel. Per-request timeout and "maximum total timeout exceeded" errors; pagination helper; resource client; connection_manager with startup, status, required, resources and tool_catalog modules; strings "required MCP servers failed to initialize" (session_init.required_mcp_wait). Plugins may declare Stdio, StreamableHttp and Sse servers (AgentPluginMcpServer). rmcp's streamable_http_server module is also linked, which suggests an MCP-server mode, but no entry point for it was found.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's gateway implements Streamable HTTP only (stdio quarantined) and plans the 2026-07-28 RC migration; Codex already negotiates that revision, so its tasks/sampling handling is a reference for the migration.

name: MCP OAuth with dynamic client registration, CIMD and issuer-change handling
what: MCP servers that need sign-in work through browser OAuth; the client discovers metadata, registers itself or uses a portable client-id document, and drops tokens if the server's issuer changes.
how: rmcp transport/auth.rs strings: "Dynamic client registration not supported", fallback to legacy OAuth endpoints derived from the base URL, authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported, "authorization server issuer changed; clearing stored credentials bound to the previous issuer", "discarding tokens but keeping portable CIMD client ID", WWW-Authenticate challenge scope handling, protected-resource metadata probe with discovery URL logging. App-server notification mcpServer/oauthLogin/completed; setting mcp_startup_authentication (prompt at startup); UI timeout "Plugin installation timed out" for OAuth during install; plugin appsNeedingAuth.
verevonRelevance: Verevon implements RFC 9728/8414/7591; add CIMD client IDs and issuer-binding of stored credentials, which Codex treats as first-class.

name: MCP server configuration surface (per server and per tool)
what: Each MCP server can be enabled or disabled, restricted to a tool allow-list, hidden from certain modes, given timeouts, an environment allow-list and per-tool approval modes.
how: Fields seen in plugin .mcp.json and config.toml schema: command, args, cwd, enabled, env, env_vars (allow-list of inherited variables), startup_timeout_sec, tool_timeout_sec (code-review 120, codex-app-tools 3600), enabled_tools, disabled_tools, omit_tools_from [deferred, code_mode], default_tools_approval_mode, tools.<name>.approval_mode (approve|prompt), tools.<name>.output_token_limit, destructive_enabled, open_world_enabled (gates tools by MCP destructive/open-world annotations), required servers (startup fails the session), bearer_token_env (HTTP auth read from an environment variable). App-server methods mcpServer/reload, mcpServer/startupStatus/updated and mcpServer/event/stream support live status.
verevonRelevance: The destructive/open-world gate and per-tool approval mode map cleanly onto Verevon's capability-binding requirement; use them to unblock the "MCP tools denied" gap with governed bindings.

name: Human-readable approval templates for connector tools
what: Before a connector action runs, the approval card says in plain language what will happen, for example "Allow GitHub to add a comment to a pull request?" with labelled parameters.
how: core/src/mcp_tool_approval_templates.rs embeds a JSON file schema_version 4 with 55 templates keyed by connector_id and tool_title; each has template ("Allow {connector_name} to create a branch?") and template_params [{name, label}] (Pull request, Repository, Comment...). Tool titles suggest GitHub-, Gmail-, Calendar-, Slack- and Drive-style tool sets (inferred; 19 templates for the largest connector id). Version mismatch is logged (expected_schema_version).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's HITL approvals should render action-specific sentences from a versioned template file per capability instead of raw tool names; this also supports Space-level policy review.
notes: Connector ids are opaque; mapping to product names is not asserted.

name: MCP Apps: tool results render interactive UIs (ext-apps standard)
what: MCP tools can return a UI resource that the chat shows as a sandboxed widget: the bundled Code Review plugin is a full pull-request workspace delivered this way.
how: code-review/server.mjs bundles @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps server helpers: registerAppTool copies _meta.ui.resourceUri to the legacy key openai/outputTemplate (and back); registerAppResource uses MIME text/html;profile=mcp-app; ui/open-link and ui/request-display-mode messages; display modes inline, fullscreen, pip; tool visibility "model" vs "app" (app-only tools hidden from the model); CSP declaration connectDomains/resourceDomains (empty means no network) and a per-view sandbox domain; host theme CSS variables; host context (locale, timeZone, userAgent, platform, container size). Plugin ships assets/pull-requests.html (776 KB), .css (1.4 MB) and .js (13.9 MB). Tool meta schema in protocol mcp-app-ui.ts accepts openai/outputTemplate, ui.resourceUri and ui/resourceUri. Resource tool descriptors also carry preferredModelDisplayMode inline|fullscreen.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's artifacts are text/HTML; adopting MCP Apps would let any capability return a governed widget (with CSP and app-only tools) without bespoke frontend work.
notes: REA analysis of the plugin directory ran (858 modules, partial graph, worker heap exhausted on server.mjs and pull-requests.js), but the facts above come from reading the unminified server.mjs.

name: MCP App sandbox host (isolated partition, port protocol, event telemetry)
what: Widgets run in a locked-down guest frame; the host exposes a narrow set of calls and logs blocked navigation, downloads and failed attaches.
how: protocol mcp-app-sandbox.ts: Electron session partition prefix codex-mcp-app-sandbox with a shared persistent partition; required frame ports navigate, notifyMcpAppsHostContext, notifyMcpAppsToolCancelled, notifyMcpAppsToolInput, notifyMcpAppsToolResult, requestMcpAppsResourceTeardown, runWidgetCode, setAdditionalGlobals, setSafeArea, setTheme, setWidgetData, setWidgetView; optional applyAutofillCandidate, getCurrentPath, notifyMcpAppsMcpNotification, prepareEnvironment, runUserCode, screenshot, stop. IPC mcp-app-sandbox-host-message and -guest-message; telemetry events mcp_app_sandbox.{attach_expired,attach_rejected,attach_unmatched,guest_attached,guest_load_failed,init_rejected,navigation_blocked,download_blocked,console_message,console_limit_reached}. mcp-app-attachment chunk persists attachments.
verevonRelevance: A host-controlled port list plus blocked-navigation/download telemetry is a concrete security checklist for rendering plugin UIs in Verevon's SolidJS shell.

name: MCP resource activity metadata (read, created, updated)
what: Tool results can declare which external resources they read, created or updated so the UI can show clickable activity chips.
how: protocol mcp-resource-activities.ts: _meta["openai/resourceActivities"] {version:1, resources:[{id, url (http/https without credentials), title, mimeType, activities: read|created|updated}]}.
verevonRelevance: Gives Verevon a standard way to surface Data Plane documents and provider actions touched by a tool call in the transcript, supporting its audit and citation UX.

name: MCP elicitation with OpenAI form extension and user verification
what: MCP servers can ask the user structured questions (forms, file pickers with options, image pickers) during a tool call and can request step-up verification.
how: Initialize capability mcpServerOpenaiFormElicitation; extension openai/elicitation form with property x-openai-input {type:file, options:[{uri,name,title,icons}], userOptions.accept}; legacy method openai/form with type openai/imagePicker; requests carry _meta.autoResolutionMs (30 000 in the template picker). codex-mcp elicitation.rs and user_verification_elicitation.rs; app-server serverRequest mcpServer/elicitation/request answered with accept/decline/cancel; second-level save prompt ("Save this reference as a reusable template?").
verevonRelevance: Elicitation is the right transport for Verevon HITL prompts raised by plugins; auto-resolution timers and decline/cancel distinctions are worth mirroring.

name: Dynamic (client-registered) tools per thread
what: The host app can register tools with the agent at thread start, optionally grouped in namespaces and loaded lazily; calls come back to the host to execute.
how: ThreadStartParams.dynamicTools[] = DynamicToolSpec {function: name, description, inputSchema, deferLoading} or {namespace, tools[]}; persisted in SQLite thread_dynamic_tools (thread_id, position, name, description, input_schema). Server request DynamicToolCallRequest (arguments, startedAtMs) answered with contentItems inputText|inputImage|inputAudio + success. The desktop's own tool bridge (codex-app-tools) is the main consumer of this mechanism.
verevonRelevance: Matches Verevon's client-supplied tools (merged as untrusted in Do mode) and adds persistence per thread, namespaces and deferral, which Verevon lacks.

name: codex-app-tools: desktop app exposed to the agent as an MCP server over a named pipe
what: The agent can manage the app itself: find, create and update chats, organise projects and the sidebar, schedule automations, manage worktrees and open panels, with approval prompts on consequential tools.
how: Plugin codex-app-tools (version 0.1.6, disabled by default and enabled by the host) runs server.mjs via a Node launcher with a six-step Node discovery chain (CODEX_MCP_NODE_PATH, CODEX_BROWSER_USE_NODE_PATH, cua_node, CODEX_CLI_PATH sibling, primary runtime cache, LOCALAPPDATA runtimes). The server forwards tools/list and tools/call over a named pipe (CODEX_APP_TOOLS_PIPE_PATH) using 4-byte little-endian length-prefixed JSON-RPC 2.0 frames (8 MiB cap) with tools/cancel on abort; request metadata keys openai/threadId, openai/toolCallId, openai/turnId or x-codex-turn-metadata; callerSource codex or chatgpt; hostId for local vs remote. .mcp.json: default_tools_approval_mode approve, approval_mode prompt for automation_update, create_thread, send_message_to_thread, fork_thread, handoff_thread, move_thread_to_project, omit_tools_from deferred, tool_timeout_sec 3600. Instructions string: "Manage the Codex desktop app: find, create, and update chats; organize projects, sidebar, and pinned items; schedule automations; manage worktrees; open app panels; and locate bundled libraries for documents, spreadsheets, slides, and PDFs."
verevonRelevance: A governed "control the product itself" tool surface (threads, projects, schedules) is the missing bridge between Verevon's chat UI actions (168 action ids, 8 model-executable) and the model; reuse the approval split (read tools auto-approved, write tools prompt).

name: Agent-editable application settings manifest
what: The agent can read and change many app preferences itself (theme, fonts, follow-up behaviour, notification rules, detail level) because each setting declares agent access in a typed manifest.
how: protocol/settings: 96 definitions created by defineConfigurationSetting (stored in config.toml), defineGlobalStateSetting and definePersistedAtomSetting; each has key, default, description, Zod schema and agentAccess hidden | read-only | read-write. toolVisibleSettingDefinitions = those not hidden; their JSON Schemas are exported to the agent (getToolVisibleSettingMetadata) with theme-id enums specialised per variant. Examples read-write: appearanceTheme, sansFontSize, followUpQueueMode, composerEnterBehavior, conversationDetailMode (STEPS_PROSE | STEPS_COMMANDS | STEPS_EXECUTION), notifications-turn-mode, reduced-motion-preference, show-context-window-usage; read-only: code-review-local-instructions, agent-usage-reset-enabled, mcp_startup_authentication; hidden: browser and Codex Micro internals.
verevonRelevance: "Settings the assistant may change on request" with a read/write/hidden classification is a cheap personalisation win for Verevon and fits its transparency goals; keep security-relevant settings read-only.
notes: Count of 96 from a node script over server.mjs lines 33170-34375.

name: Connectors: ChatGPT apps surfaced to the agent through the codex_apps MCP server
what: Account-level connectors (GitHub, Gmail, Drive, Slack and others) appear to the agent as tools; if the bridge is down the agent is told it is unavailable.
how: A built-in MCP server named codex_apps carries connector tools; app-server app/list, app/list/updated notification, AppSummary/AppBranding (category, website, privacy policy, terms, isDiscoverableApp); codex-connectors crate (directory_cache.rs, connector_runtime/persistence.rs) and ext/connectors plugin_app.rs for plugin-declared apps ("plugin app config is missing an app id"); error "codex_apps MCP server is unavailable"; tool disk cache CodexAppsToolsDiskCache; plugin install triggers a codex_apps cache refresh and appsNeedingAuth check.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's integration-corev2 provider actions are the analogue; exposing them to the model through a single governed bridge with a disk/tool cache would unify chat and Do mode.
notes: Cloud-side behaviour not observable.

name: Tool-call result annotations: truncation and source metadata
what: Tool outputs carry markers when they were truncated and which sources produced them so clients can show what the model actually saw.
how: ResponseItem fields tool_result_sources, tool_result_metadata, _codex_executed_tool_call_truncated {original_bytes, max_bytes, omitted_calls, original_name_bytes}; MCP output_token_limit per tool; hook output spill to files; code-mode max_output_tokens (default 10000).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's result handles (result_query) already solve large outputs; surfacing explicit truncation metadata in the transcript would improve trust.

name: App-server: JSON-RPC protocol between every client and the Rust agent runtime
what: The desktop app, terminal UI, IDE clients and other front ends all talk to one Rust process (codex app-server) through a typed JSON-RPC API; the UI never embeds the agent loop.
how: Method families (client requests): initialize with clientInfo and InitializeCapabilities {experimentalApi, optOutNotificationMethods, explicitGatewayOauth, requestAttestation, mcpServerOpenaiFormElicitation, extensions}; thread/{start,read,list,fork,resume,archive,unarchive,delete,search,compact/start,revert,rollback,queue/*,goal/*,attachment/*,metadata/update,settings/update,shellCommand,inject_items,approveGuardianDeniedAction}; turn/{start,steer,interrupt}; review/start; command/exec; fs/{readFile,writeFile,readDirectory,getMetadata,createDirectory,copy,remove,watch}; config/{read,value/write,batchWrite}; configRequirements/read; model/list; modelProvider/capabilities/read; collaborationMode/list; permissionProfile/list; experimentalFeature/list; account/*; plugin/*, marketplace/*, skills/*, hooks/list, app/list, mcpServer*; memory/{status,reset}; feedback/upload; project/*; environment/{add,info}; remoteControl/*; userVerification/*; realtime/*. ThreadStartParams has 27 fields including model, modelProvider, serviceTier, cwd, approvalPolicy, approvalsReviewer, sandbox, personality, dynamicTools, selectedCapabilityRoots, allowProviderModelFallback, historyMode, sessionStartSource. UserInput variants: Text, Image, LocalImage, Audio, LocalAudio, Skill, Mention. The Electron app warms a fixed set of discovery methods (app/list, config/read, hooks/list, model/list, plugin/list, skills/list...) with tracing.
verevonRelevance: Integration Core already runs the official Codex app-server for BYO ChatGPT; this surface shows what a first-party Verevon "session protocol" (threads, turns, items, approvals) should expose so web, CLI and future clients share one runtime.
notes: Method names from string literals; request/response schemas were not read except those bundled in server.mjs and the plugin protocol modules.

name: App-server notification catalogue with per-client opt-in and opt-out
what: Clients subscribe only to the events they render: a web view opts in to streaming deltas and approvals, while legacy raw events can be opted out to save bandwidth.
how: protocol/src/mcp.ts defines APP_SERVER_NOTIFICATION_OPT_IN: about 150 methods mapped to a boolean (handled in the webview or not). Examples true: thread/started, thread/name/updated, thread/queue/changed, thread/tokenUsage/updated, turn/started, hook/started, hook/completed, turn/completed, turn/diff/updated, turn/plan/updated, item/started, item/completed, item/agentMessage/delta, item/plan/delta, item/reasoning/summaryTextDelta, item/reasoning/textDelta, item/commandExecution/outputDelta, item/fileChange/patchUpdated, item/autoApprovalReview/started|completed, autoApprovalReview/strictReviewRequired, item/mcpToolCall/progress, mcpServer/startupStatus/updated, account/rateLimits/updated, app/list/updated, skills/changed, model/rerouted, model/verification, model/safetyBuffering/updated, guardianWarning, windowsSandbox/setupCompleted. Raw and legacy codex/event/* mirrors (about 70) default to false; collab_agent_* spawn, interaction, waiting, resume and close events are true. APP_SERVER_NOTIFICATION_METHODS_TO_OPT_OUT is computed from the false entries (except connection-internal fs/changed and process output).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's AG-UI/SSE stream could publish an explicit event catalogue with opt-in flags per client type (web, CLI, mobile) to keep payloads small and contracts testable.

name: App-server transports and connection auth (stdio, unix socket, WebSocket)
what: The runtime can run as a child process over stdio, as a local daemon over a unix socket with WebSocket upgrade, or as a network service over WebSocket with token or signed-JWT auth.
how: app-server-transport crate: transport/stdio.rs, unix_socket.rs ("control socket acceptor", websocket upgrade), remote_control controller/server_api (enrollment and server refresh checks server_id/environment_id), connection_auth.rs, daemon_shutdown.rs (CODEX_DAEMON_SHUTDOWN_FILE). CLI flags --listen and --ws-auth {capability-token | signed-bearer-token}; capability-token requires --ws-token-file or --ws-token-sha256 (hex SHA-256 of the token); signed-bearer-token requires --ws-shared-secret-file plus optional --ws-issuer, --ws-audience, --ws-max-clock-skew-seconds and validates exp/nbf/iss/aud JWT claims; non-loopback websocket without auth is refused ("configure --ws-auth"). app-server-daemon crate ("Codex App Server Daemon", daemon_auto_start feature, "local daemon requires a Unix socket"). In-process app-server client also exists (app-server-client).
verevonRelevance: The capability-token-by-hash and signed-JWT modes give a ready recipe for authenticating browser sandboxes or remote devices to Verevon runtimes without sharing raw secrets.

name: Schema-first SDK support, experimental gating and version negotiation
what: Client libraries can be generated from the runtime's own types; unstable methods require an explicit opt-in capability; clients check server version before using newer features.
how: CLI subcommands generate-ts, generate-json-schema and generate-internal-json-schema (and app-server-test-client). Methods flagged experimental fail with "requires experimentalApi capability"; ThreadStartParams includes mockExperimentalField and experimentalRawEvents for tests. protocol app-server-min-version.ts, app-server-version.ts and app-server-feature-support.ts; the desktop checks features such as pluginMcpConfigOverrides by comparing the connected app-server version (Ti(appServerVersion, "pluginMcpConfigOverrides")). Runtime user-agent strings show version 0.162.0-alpha.1 (digits after "alpha.1" are ambiguous in the concatenated literal).
verevonRelevance: Verevon already publishes OpenAPI and a generated SDK; adding an explicit experimental capability gate and server-version feature checks would let the web app and CLI evolve independently.

name: Execution hosts: local, SSH, WSL and remote-control devices with environments
what: A task can run on this PC, in WSL, over SSH or on another enrolled device; each has its own app-server connection, filesystem and skill/plugin settings.
how: protocol host-config.ts: host kinds local, ssh, wsl, remote-control (isRemoteHostConfig). exec-server crate (environment.rs, resolved_capability.rs, capability_discovery(.cache).rs, rpc.rs, client.rs) provides executor-side filesystem, process and capability discovery; thread start takes selectedCapabilityRoots and environments; environment/add and environment/info; a model tool waits for an environment marked "starting"; executor-bound skills require an environment. Remote control: enrollments and device-key bindings in SQLite (remote_control_enrollments, device_key_bindings), pairing/start|status, enable/disable, client/list; settings keepRemoteControlAwakeWhilePluggedIn.

name: Automations: scheduled and recurring agent tasks stored as TOML with SQLite run history

name: Automation run contract: per-automation memory file and mandatory inbox directive
what: Every automation run keeps notes in a memory file and ends with a one-line structured summary that becomes the user's inbox entry.
how: System prompt text injected for automation runs: read and update $CODEX_HOME/automations/<automation_id>/memory.md (created if missing; read first to avoid repeating work; write a concise summary and run time before finishing); the response MUST end with exactly one remark directive ::inbox-item{title="..." summary="..."} on its own line (no commas between args); title 4-8 words saying what the thread now is, summary 6-14 words with next step or blocker; absolute file links; add label codex-automation when an automation opens a PR; avoid asking the user for more input. The directive is parsed by the renderer (inbox-items-create).
verevonRelevance: A strict machine-readable run footer plus a per-job memory file is a simple way to make Verevon scheduled runs produce findings/reports and avoid repeated work; fits the planned Findings/Routines pages.

name: Automation inbox, run threads and heartbeat automations
what: Each automation run is a real conversation thread; results land in an Inbox with read state and archive reasons. A heartbeat automation wakes an existing thread on a schedule instead of starting new ones.
how: automation_runs(thread_id PRIMARY KEY, automation_id, status, read_at, thread_title, source_cwd, inbox_title, inbox_summary, archived_user_message, archived_assistant_message, archived_reason, created_at, updated_at). Kinds cron (new thread per run, optional auto_archive) and heartbeat (target_thread_id). Inbox UI strings: scheduled task details, next run, run now ("Could not start scheduled task"), Active/Paused/Completed. Deterministic per-install jitter: sha256(salt:id:time) mod 601 minus 300 seconds using a persisted .run-jitter-salt file to avoid thundering-herd start times.
verevonRelevance: The jitter salt and thread-per-run inbox model are cheap improvements for Verevon's cron sweeper and findings page; heartbeat targets fit long-running research threads.

name: Context compaction controls and hooks

name: Interactive request tools and plan mode (request_user_input, update_plan)

name: Guardian v2: asynchronous security reviewer that gates later actions
what: A small reviewer model watches the agent's trajectory without blocking, scoring risk; a "high" score switches future actions to a blocking review. Evidence from tool output, skills and plugin descriptions is treated as untrusted.
how: ext/guardian-v2 (async_scorer approval/authorization/classification, sync_reviewer): GuardianV2Config {async_classifier_mode, async_classifier_conversation_token_limit, enabled, free_guardian, persist_scores, classifier_instructions, review_threshold (0..1), max_tool_call_lag, reasoning_effort, max_action_tokens, reuse_parent_compaction, review_scope computer_use_only | sandboxed_exec_commands, transcript sources tool_calls/tool_outputs/reasoning with entry token caps}. name: Deep research as a skill-only plugin: dedicated worker, source ledger, cited DOCX

name: First-run onboarding as a plan-driven skill with native request surfaces

name: Code Review as an MCP App: PR workspace, private reviews and chat-bound reviews
what: A bundled plugin turns the chat into a pull-request cockpit (list, diff, checks, comments, merge) and can run a private AI review of a PR without cloning it, returning ranked findings.

name: Computer Use confirmation policy shipped as readable data
what: Windows control follows a four-tier confirmation policy that classifies actions into hand-off, always-confirm, pre-approvable and no-confirmation, with numbered action classes and a rule that third-party content never grants permission.

SKILL.md requires reading guidance.md and confirmations.md before acting; the browser plugin lists confirmations as required for tab_cdp_call and webmcp_invoke_tool via documents.json.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's browser grants and Do-mode HITL could adopt a numbered, versioned confirmation taxonomy stored as data (evaluated by the policy gate) instead of a substring risk list.

name: Review agent: explicit-only system skill with a strict finding standard
what: Delegated code reviews run through a read-only skill that returns only findings the author would fix, ranked P0 to P3, and says "No findings." rather than inventing issues.

name: Desktop process model: Electron main, sandboxed renderer, workers and a chunked message bridge
what: The desktop shell is thin: the renderer talks to the main process through one message channel with chunking and acknowledgements, heavy work runs in workers, and the agent runs in a separate Rust process.
how: IPC literals codex_desktop:message-for-view, message-from-view, chunked-message-ack, worker:*, connect-app-host in bootstrap; protocol chunked-message-protocol.ts and chunked-message-receiver.ts split large payloads; workers for git, computer-use (capture, skysight), open-in; vscode-capn-rpc-message.ts wraps Cap'n Web RPC messages (sessionId, connect/message) for editor extension bridges; separate processes: codex app-server, code-mode host, command runner, sandbox service, node_repl; IPC handlers check the sender with isTrustedIpcEvent/isTrustedIpcSender (the scout's REA run counted 15 sender-validation sites).

name: Plugin servers are built from the same monorepo schemas (shared protocol package)
what: First-party plugin servers reuse the app's Zod schemas and helper modules, so tool inputs, settings and host protocol cannot drift from the app.
how: server.mjs files are single-file bundles with source-path comments: ../bundled-plugins/codex-app-tools/src/server.ts imports ../protocol/src/host-config.ts and dynamic-app-tools.ts; code-review bundles more than 280 modules from the app protocol, shared-node and git-worker packages plus ../../codex/codex-apps/protocol/src, shared-node/src/github, git-worker, @openai/pull-requests-bridge and @modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps; plugin.json versions track the app release (26.1007.21434) for desktop-coupled plugins and independent semver for content plugins (deep-research 0.1.1, latex 0.2.8, visualize 1.0.49).

name: Plugin permission model is implicit: no per-plugin capability grants observed
what: Plugins declare what they are (capabilities labels, MCP servers, hooks) but nothing in the manifest grants or limits OS or data access; safety comes from per-tool approvals, sandbox policy, environment allow-lists and admin requirements.
how: plugin.json interface.capabilities is a display label set (Interactive, Read, Write); .mcp.json controls env_vars allow-list (for example code-review passes GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, CODEX_API_KEY, proxy variables), default_tools_approval_mode and per-tool approval_mode; hooks need trust; marketplace policy gates install/auth; admin requirements can disable plugins or restrict hooks; no field found for filesystem, network or data-scope grants per plugin. Plugin MCP servers launch as ordinary child processes (cmd.exe, node) of the app.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should do better: require plugin manifests to declare data scopes and capability classes that the capability-policy gate enforces, instead of relying on approval prompts.
notes: Inference from the absence of such fields in nine manifests and the config schema; cloud-side plugin review is not visible. Quality 2 reflects the weak isolation, not the packaging.

name: Personality and profile presets

name: Tool registry hygiene: collision errors, schema size caps and namespaces

how: ToolRegistryConfig: error_on_tool_collisions, excluded tool namespaces, direct_only tools (never deferred), tool_input_schema max bytes, turn_metadata_includes_tool_info; dynamic tools namespace spec; MCP tools exposed as normalised identifiers (mcp__server__tool); skills.read/list as tools skills.* namespace; tool_namespace in multi-agent config.

notes: Key names read from concatenated config strings.

name: Unified computer-use plugin: one REPL, selectable browser and desktop surfaces
what: A single JavaScript session can drive either the in-app browser, the desktop (via the sky package) or both; the host chooses which surfaces and browser backends are active.
how: Host logic builds the cua_repl server definition: surfaces browser maps to @oai/browser-desktop/service and computer maps to @oai/sky/service (JSON in an environment variable), CUA_REPL_ENABLED_SURFACES lists them, browser backends are passed via env, command/args point to @oai/cua-repl/bin/cua-repl.mjs inside the primary runtime node_modules; enablement requires the Node REPL and at least one surface; plugin hook calls cua_repl.turn_ended on Interrupt, SubagentStop and Stop. Native Office apps show as "Live workbook / presentation / document control" in the Computer Use settings.
verevonRelevance: One runtime with pluggable surfaces and a turn-ended cleanup hook is the clean way to give Verevon's agent browser plus desktop control through the same governed capability.
notes: Browser internals belong to the in-app browser audit.

name: Worktree tasks with local-to-worktree handoff and rollback
what: A task can move its git state between the local checkout and an isolated worktree; failures are rolled back and explained step by step.
how: protocol worktree.ts (worktree names: 1-64 chars, lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens, hex IDs and Windows device names reserved), host-worktree-settings, worktree-path-matching, thread attachment owners; UI flows moveToWorktree and moveToLocal with specific errors (branch checked out elsewhere, local tracked changes, source stash apply failed, rollback failed), thread handoff tool handoff_thread in codex-app-tools, archived worktree cleanup, CLI flags --worktree for new sessions and fork; app-server project and environment APIs; automations can run in worktree or local.
verevonRelevance: Space workspaces with promotion (Verevon's PromoteWorkspace overlay merge) have the same need for explicit handoff failure states and rollback.

name: Feedback and performance-trace upload with explicit consent and correlation IDs
what: Users can send feedback with logs or record a performance trace; the app states what will be uploaded, lets them keep it local, and issues a Feedback ID that survives failed uploads.
how: /feedback command and feedback/upload RPC; dialog strings: Feedback ID, uploading, upload incomplete, upload not confirmed (warns against duplicates), disabled by configuration; trace recording flow: start details, note field, "Send profile trace?" warning that JS and native memory-allocation profiles may contain sensitive data, Keep local, Show local trace; debug RAM indicator by process type (main, helpers, App Server, rollout children).
verevonRelevance: Verevon's audit and support tooling can copy the consent wording, the idempotent Feedback ID and the "not confirmed, may duplicate" state.
notes: Evidence is the renderer string catalogue; the feedback/upload RPC name comes from the codex.exe method list.

name: Diagnostics commands and config warnings
what: Users can inspect effective configuration, retained warnings, process lists and session status from commands, and are shown config and deprecation warnings as notifications.
how: Commands /status (session configuration and token usage), /debug-config (layers and requirement sources), /warnings (retained warnings and diagnostic details), /ps and /stop (background terminals), /rollout (print rollout file path), a codex doctor update-check module (cli/src/doctor/updates.rs), notifications configWarning, deprecationNotice, guardianWarning, windows/worldWritableWarning; thread/backgroundTerminals/list; config load errors surfaced with file context (config-load-error.ts).
verevonRelevance: A /debug-config style "why is this setting active" view backed by the layer stack is a high-value transparency feature for Verevon's instruction hierarchy.

name: Customizable keymaps and terminal chrome (TUI)
what: Every terminal action (chat, list, pager, agents, editor, global) can be remapped, and the status line, title, theme and pets are configurable.
how: Config [tui] with keymap tables: TuiChatKeymap (toggle_voice, interrupt_turn, increase/decrease_reasoning_effort, previous/next_permission_mode, edit_queued_message, skip_question...), TuiListKeymap, TuiPagerKeymap, TuiAgentsKeymap (resume, search, new_task, new_worktree, fork, rename, stop, archive, delete), TuiEditorKeymap (17 editing actions), TuiGlobalKeymap (open_agents, open_transcript, toggle_fast_mode, toggle_raw_output, toggle_side_conversation, toggle_vim_mode...); options such as animations, show_tooltips, auto_recap, vim_mode_default, raw_output_mode, fullscreen_transcript, mouse_scroll_speed, terminal_title and status_line items; /keymap, /vim, /theme, /statusline, /title.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a CLI/TUI product shell (GOAL.md), this keymap schema and per-context action names are a ready spec; for the web UI the keymap protocol still applies to a shortcut sheet.

name: Licensing split across shipped extensibility assets
what: The curated skill pack carries an Apache-2.0 licence file, while every bundled plugin manifest is marked Proprietary and the Rust runtime links Apache/MIT crates.
how: resources/skills/skills/.curated/hatch-pet/LICENSE.txt is the Apache License 2.0; plugin.json license field is "Proprietary" for browser, chrome, code-review, codex-app-tools, computer-use, deep-research and visualize; latex lists third-party notices and DEPENDENCIES.md; codex.exe embeds licence headers of Rust dependencies (Apache and MIT); resources/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt lists JavaScript dependencies only.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's licence gate (Apache vendorable, MIT portable, proprietary shapes only) applies: reuse designs and wire formats, but do not copy bundled plugin code, skill prose or the guardian prompt verbatim without a licence check.
notes: Whether the open-source Codex CLI repository covers the app-server crates is outside this evidence (INF: it is public under Apache-2.0).
